              - paragraph [ref=e1725]:
                - text: The shape and structure of cats' cheeks is insufficient to allow them to take in liquids using suction. Lapping at a rate of four times a second, the cat touches the smooth tip of its tongue to the surface of the water, and quickly retracts it like a corkscrew, drawing water upward into their mouths.
                - superscript [ref=e1726]:
                  - link "[140]" [ref=e1727] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Reis_2010-141"
                - superscript [ref=e1729]:
                  - link "[141]" [ref=e1730] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Kim_2012-142"
              - paragraph [ref=e1732]:
                - text: Feral cats and free-fed house cats consume several small meals in a day. The frequency and size of meals varies between individuals. They select food based on its temperature, smell, and texture; they dislike chilled foods and respond most strongly to moist foods rich in amino acids, which are similar to meat. Cats reject novel flavors (a response termed
                - link "neophobia" [ref=e1733] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neophobia
                - text: ) and learn quickly to
                - link "avoid foods that have tasted unpleasant" [ref=e1734] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conditioned_taste_aversion
                - text: in the past.
                - superscript [ref=e1735]:
                  - link "[107]" [ref=e1736] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Bradshaw-108"
                - superscript [ref=e1738]:
                  - link "[142]" [ref=e1739] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Zaghini-143"
                - text: It is also a common misconception that all cats like milk or cream, as they tend to avoid sweet food and milk. Most adult cats are
                - link "lactose intolerant" [ref=e1741] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lactose_intolerant
                - text: ; the sugar in milk is not easily digested and may cause soft stools or
                - link "diarrhea" [ref=e1742] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diarrhea
                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e1743]:
                  - link "[143]" [ref=e1744] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Kienzle_1994-144"
                - text: Some also develop odd eating habits and like to eat or chew on things such as wool, plastic, cables, paper, string, aluminum foil, or even coal. This condition,
                - link "pica" [ref=e1746] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pica_(disorder)
                - text: ", can threaten their health, depending on the amount and toxicity of the items eaten."
                - superscript [ref=e1747]:
                  - link "[144]" [ref=e1748] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Bradshaw_1997-145"
              - paragraph [ref=e1750]:
                - text: Cats hunt small prey, primarily birds and rodents,
                - superscript [ref=e1751]:
                  - link "[145]" [ref=e1752] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Woods-146"
                - text: and are often used as a form of pest control.
                - superscript [ref=e1754]:
                  - link "[146]" [ref=e1755] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-147"
                - superscript [ref=e1757]:
                  - link "[147]" [ref=e1758] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-148"
                - text: Other common small creatures, such as lizards, snakes and insects, may also become prey.
                - superscript [ref=e1760]:
                  - link "[148]" [ref=e1761] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-149"
                - superscript [ref=e1763]:
                  - link "[149]" [ref=e1764] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-150"
                - text: Cats use two hunting strategies, either stalking prey actively, or
                - link "waiting in ambush" [ref=e1766] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambush_predator
                - text: until a prey animal comes close enough to be captured.
                - superscript [ref=e1767]:
                  - link "[150]" [ref=e1768] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-How_Cats_Evolved_to_Win_the_Internet-151"
                - text: The strategy used depends on available prey, with cats waiting in ambush outside burrows, but tending to actively stalk birds.
                - superscript [ref=e1770]:
                  - link "[151]" [ref=e1771] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Turner_2000-152"
                - superscript [ref=e1773]:
                  - 'generic "Page / location: 153" [ref=e1774]': ": 153"
                - text: Domestic cats are a major
                - link "predators of wildlife" [ref=e1775] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_predation_on_wildlife
                - text: in the United States, killing an estimated 1.3 to 4.0 billion birds and 6.3 to 22.3 billion mammals annually.
                - superscript [ref=e1776]:
                  - link "[152]" [ref=e1777] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-NC012913-153"
              - paragraph [ref=e1779]:
                - text: Certain species appear more susceptible than others; in one English village, for example, 30% of house sparrow mortality was linked to the domestic cat.
                - superscript [ref=e1780]:
                  - link "[153]" [ref=e1781] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Chucher_1987-154"
                - text: In the recovery of ringed robins (
                - link "Erithacus rubecula" [ref=e1784] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erithacus_rubecula
                - text: ) and dunnocks (
                - link "Prunella modularis" [ref=e1786] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prunella_modularis
                - text: ) in Britain, 31% of deaths were a result of cat predation.
                - superscript [ref=e1787]:
                  - link "[154]" [ref=e1788] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Mead_1982_183–186-155"
                - text: In parts of North America, the presence of larger carnivores such as
                - link "coyotes" [ref=e1790] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coyote
                - text: ", which prey on cats and other small predators, reduces the effect of predation by cats and other small predators such as"
                - link "opossums" [ref=e1791] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opossum
                - text: and
                - link "raccoons" [ref=e1792] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raccoon
                - text: on bird numbers and variety.
                - superscript [ref=e1793]:
                  - link "[155]" [ref=e1794] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Crooks_1999-156"
              - paragraph [ref=e1796]:
                - text: Another poorly understood element of cat hunting behavior is the presentation of prey to human guardians. One explanation is that cats adopt humans into their social group and share excess kill with others in the group according to the
                - link "dominance hierarchy" [ref=e1797] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominance_hierarchy
                - text: ", in which humans are reacted to as if they are at or near the top."
                - superscript [ref=e1798]:
                  - link "[156]" [ref=e1799] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Leyhausen_1978-157"
                - text: Another explanation is that they attempt to teach their guardians to hunt or to help their human as if feeding "an elderly cat, or an inept kitten".
                - superscript [ref=e1801]:
                  - link "[157]" [ref=e1802] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Morris_Catwatching_1-158"
                - text: This hypothesis is inconsistent with the fact that male cats also bring home prey, though males have negligible involvement in raising kittens.
                - superscript [ref=e1804]:
                  - link "[151]" [ref=e1805] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Turner_2000-152"
                - superscript [ref=e1807]:
                  - 'generic "Page / location: 153" [ref=e1808]': ": 153"
            - region [ref=e1809]:
              - heading "Fighting" [level=3] [ref=e1811]
              - figure [ref=e1812]:
                - link [ref=e1813] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GAto.jpg
                - generic [ref=e1815]:
                  - text: A domestic cat exhibiting a
                  - link "threat display" [ref=e1816] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deimatic_behaviour
                  - text: ", hissing and arching its back."
              - paragraph [ref=e1817]:
                - text: Domestic males are more likely to fight than females.
                - superscript [ref=e1818]:
                  - link "[158]" [ref=e1819] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Lindell-159"
                - text: The most common reason for feral
                - link "cat fighting" [ref=e1821] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catfight_(animal_behavior)
                - text: is competition between two males to mate with a female, and most fights are won by the heavier male.
                - superscript [ref=e1822]:
                  - link "[159]" [ref=e1823] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-courtship-160"
                - text: Another common reason for fighting in domestic cats is the difficulty of establishing territories within a small home.
                - superscript [ref=e1825]:
                  - link "[158]" [ref=e1826] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Lindell-159"
                - text: Female cats also fight over territory or to defend their kittens.
                - link "Neutering" [ref=e1828] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutering
                - text: decreases or eliminates this behavior in many cases, suggesting that the behavior is linked to
                - link "sex hormones" [ref=e1829] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_hormone
                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e1830]:
                  - link "[160]" [ref=e1831] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Kustritz2007-161"
              - paragraph [ref=e1833]:
                - text: When cats become aggressive, they try to appear larger and more threatening by raising their fur, arching their backs, turning sideways, hissing, or spitting.
                - superscript [ref=e1834]:
                  - link "[161]" [ref=e1835] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-behaviourguide-162"
                - text: Often, the ears are pointed down and back to avoid damage to the inner ear and potentially listen for any changes behind them while focused forward. Cats may also vocalize loudly and bare their teeth in an effort to further intimidate their opponents. Fights usually consist of grappling, slapping the face and body with the forepaws, and bites. Cats throw themselves to the ground in a defensive posture to rake their opponent's belly with their hind legs.
                - superscript [ref=e1837]:
                  - link "[162]" [ref=e1838] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-163"
              - paragraph [ref=e1840]:
                - text: Serious damage is rare, because the fights are usually short, with the loser fleeing with scratches to the face and ears. More severe fights for mating rights may give deep punctures and lacerations. Normally, serious injuries from fighting are limited to infections from scratches and bites. Bites are probably the main route of transmission of the
                - link "feline immunodeficiency virus" [ref=e1841] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feline_immunodeficiency_virus
                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e1842]:
                  - link "[163]" [ref=e1843] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Pederson_1989-164"
                - text: Sexually active males are usually involved in many fights and have battered faces;
                - superscript [ref=e1845]:
                  - link "[164]" [ref=e1846] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-165"
                - text: to protect against facial injuries during fights, intact adult male cats often develop prominent cheeks due to the influence of testosterone as
                - link "secondary sex characteristics" [ref=e1848] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_sex_characteristic
                - text: ", which also signal to females that the cat is a potential mate."
                - superscript [ref=e1849]:
                  - link "[165]" [ref=e1850] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-166"
                - text: Cats often threaten animals larger than them to defend their territory, such as dogs and
                - link "foxes" [ref=e1852] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_fox
                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e1853]:
                  - link "[166]" [ref=e1854] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-167"
            - region [ref=e1856]:
              - heading "Reproduction" [level=3] [ref=e1858]

                  - text: known as
                  - link "lordosis behavior" [ref=e1864] [cursor=pointer]:

                  - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=e1865]:
                - text: The cat secretes and perceives
                - link "pheromones" [ref=e1866] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pheromone
                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e1867]:
                  - link "[167]" [ref=e1868] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Bland1979-168"
                - text: Female cats, called queens, are
                - link "polyestrous" [ref=e1870] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyestrous
                - text: with several
                - link "estrus" [ref=e1871] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estrus
                - text: cycles during a year, lasting usually 21 days. They are usually ready to mate between early February and August
                - superscript [ref=e1872]:
                  - link "[168]" [ref=e1873] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Jemmett1977-169"
                - text: in northern temperate zones and throughout the year in equatorial regions.
                - superscript [ref=e1875]:
                  - link "[169]" [ref=e1876] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-estrous_cycle-170"
              - paragraph [ref=e1878]:
                - text: Several males, called tomcats, are attracted to a female in heat. They fight over her, and the victor wins the right to mate. At first, the female rejects the male, but eventually, the female allows the male to mate. The female utters a loud yowl as the male pulls out of her because a male cat's
                - link "penis" [ref=e1879] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penis
                - text: has a band of about 120–150 backward-pointing
                - link "penile spines" [ref=e1880] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penile_spines
                - text: ", which are about 1 mm (0.04 in) long; upon withdrawal of the penis, the spines may provide the female with increased sexual stimulation, which acts to"
                - link "induce ovulation" [ref=e1881] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Induced_ovulation_(animals)
                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e1882]:
                  - link "[170]" [ref=e1883] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Aronson_1967-171"
              - figure "In this radiography of a pregnant cat, the skeletons of two fetuses are on the left and right of the uterus." [ref=e1885]:
                - link [ref=e1886] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Radiography_of_a_pregnant_cat.jpg
              - paragraph [ref=e1889]:
                - text: After mating, the female cleans her
                - link "vulva" [ref=e1890] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulva
                - text: thoroughly. If a male attempts to mate with her at this point, the female attacks him. After about 20 to 30 minutes, once the female is finished grooming, the cycle will repeat.
                - superscript [ref=e1891]:
                  - link "[171]" [ref=e1892] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-compendium-172"
                - text: Because ovulation is not always triggered by a single mating, females may not be impregnated by the first male with which they mate.
                - superscript [ref=e1894]:
                  - link "[172]" [ref=e1895] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Wildt_1980-173"
                - text: Furthermore, cats are
                - link "superfecund" [ref=e1897] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfecundation
                - text: ; that is, a female may mate with more than one male when she is in heat, with the result that different kittens in a litter may have different fathers.
                - superscript [ref=e1898]:
                  - link "[171]" [ref=e1899] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-compendium-172"
              - paragraph [ref=e1901]:
                - text: The
                - link "morula" [ref=e1902] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morula
                - text: forms 124 hours after conception. At 148 hours, early
                - link "blastocysts" [ref=e1903] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blastocyst
                - text: form. At 10–12 days, implantation occurs.
                - superscript [ref=e1904]:
                  - link "[173]" [ref=e1905] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-174"
                - text: The
                - link "gestation" [ref=e1907] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gestation
                - text: of queens lasts between 64 and 67 days, with an average of 65 days.
                - superscript [ref=e1908]:
                  - link "[168]" [ref=e1909] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Jemmett1977-169"
                - superscript [ref=e1911]:
                  - link "[174]" [ref=e1912] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Tsutsui_1993-175"
              - figure "Two 17-day-old kittens" [ref=e1914]:
                - link [ref=e1915] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:പൂച്ചക്കുഞ്ഞുങ്ങൾ_(17_ദിവസം_പ്രായം).JPG
              - paragraph [ref=e1918]:
                - text: Based on a study of 2,300 free-ranging queens conducted from May 1998 and October2000, they had one to six kittens per
                - link "litter" [ref=e1920] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litter_(animal)
                - text: ", with an average of three kittens. They produced a mean of 1.4 litters per year, but a maximum of three litters in a year. Of 169 kittens, 127 died before they were six months old due to a trauma caused in most cases by dog attacks and road accidents."
                - superscript [ref=e1921]:
                  - link "[175]" [ref=e1922] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Nutter2004-176"
                - text: The first litter is usually smaller than subsequent litters. Kittens are weaned between six and seven weeks of age. Queens normally reach sexual maturity at 5–10 months, and males at 5–7 months. This varies depending on breed.
                - superscript [ref=e1924]:
                  - link "[171]" [ref=e1925] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-compendium-172"
                - text: Kittens reach
                - link "puberty" [ref=e1927] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puberty
                - text: at the age of 9–10 months.
                - superscript [ref=e1928]:
                  - link "[168]" [ref=e1929] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Jemmett1977-169"
              - paragraph [ref=e1931]:
                - text: Cats are ready to go to new homes at about 12 weeks of age, when they are ready to leave their mother.
                - superscript [ref=e1932]:
                  - link "[176]" [ref=e1933] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-177"
                - text: They can be surgically
                - link "sterilized" [ref=e1935] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutering
                - text: (spayed or
                - link "castrated" [ref=e1936] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castration
                - text: ) as early as seven weeks to limit unwanted reproduction.
                - superscript [ref=e1937]:
                  - link "[177]" [ref=e1938] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-178"
                - text: This surgery also prevents undesirable sex-related behavior, such as aggression,
                - link "territory marking" [ref=e1940] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spraying_(animal_behavior)
                - text: (spraying urine) in males, and yowling (calling) in females. Traditionally, this surgery was performed at around six to nine months of age, but it is increasingly being performed before
                - link "puberty" [ref=e1941] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puberty
                - text: ", at about three to six months."
                - superscript [ref=e1942]:
                  - link "[160]" [ref=e1943] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Kustritz2007-161"
                - text: In the United States, about 80% of household cats are neutered.
                - superscript [ref=e1945]:
                  - link "[178]" [ref=e1946] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-179"
          - region [ref=e1948]:
            - heading "Lifespan and health" [level=2] [ref=e1950]
            - note [ref=e1951]:
              - text: "Main articles:"
              - link "Cat health" [ref=e1952] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_health
              - text: and
              - link "Aging in cats" [ref=e1953] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aging_in_cats
            - paragraph [ref=e1954]:
              - text: The average lifespan of pet cats has risen in recent decades. In the early 1980s, it was about 7 years,
              - superscript [ref=e1955]:
                - link "[179]" [ref=e1956] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Kraft1998-180"
              - superscript [ref=e1958]:
                - 'generic "Page / location: 33" [ref=e1959]': ": 33"
              - superscript [ref=e1960]:
                - link "[180]" [ref=e1961] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Nassar_1984-181"
              - text: rising to 9.4 years in 1995
              - superscript [ref=e1963]:
                - link "[179]" [ref=e1964] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Kraft1998-180"
              - superscript [ref=e1966]:
                - 'generic "Page / location: 33" [ref=e1967]': ": 33"
              - text: and an average of about 13 years as of 2014 and 2023.
              - superscript [ref=e1968]:
                - link "[181]" [ref=e1969] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-182"
              - superscript [ref=e1971]:
                - link "[182]" [ref=e1972] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-183"
            - paragraph [ref=e1974]:
              - text: Neutering increases life expectancy; one 2024 study found neutered cats to live one year longer than intact cats.
              - superscript [ref=e1975]:
                - link "[183]" [ref=e1976] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-184"
              - text: Having a cat
              - link "neutered" [ref=e1978] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutering
              - text: confers some health benefits, such as a decreased incidence of reproductive
              - link "neoplasia" [ref=e1979] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasia
              - text: .
              - superscript [ref=e1980]:
                - link "[184]" [ref=e1981] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Obesity1-185"
              - text: However, neutering decreases metabolism
              - superscript [ref=e1983]:
                - link "[185]" [ref=e1984] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-186"
              - superscript [ref=e1986]:
                - link "[186]" [ref=e1987] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Obesity2-187"
              - superscript [ref=e1989]:
                - link "[187]" [ref=e1990] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Obesity3-188"
              - text: and increases food intake,
              - superscript [ref=e1992]:
                - link "[187]" [ref=e1993] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Obesity3-188"
              - superscript [ref=e1995]:
                - link "[188]" [ref=e1996] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Obesity4-189"
              - text: both of which can cause obesity in neutered cats.
              - superscript [ref=e1998]:
                - link "[189]" [ref=e1999] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Obesity5-190"
              - text: Pre-pubertal neutering (neutering at 4 months or earlier) was only recommended by 28% of American veterinarians in one study. Some concerns of early neutering were metabolic, retarded
              - link "physeal closure" [ref=e2001] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epiphyseal_plate
              - text: ", and urinary tract disease related."
              - superscript [ref=e2002]:
                - link "[190]" [ref=e2003] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-191"
            - region [ref=e2005]:
              - heading "Disease" [level=3] [ref=e2007]
              - note [ref=e2008]:
                - text: "Main article:"

              - paragraph [ref=e2010]:
                - text: About 250 heritable
                - link "genetic disorders" [ref=e2011] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder
                - text: have been identified in cats; many are similar to human
                - link "inborn errors of metabolism" [ref=e2012] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inborn_errors_of_metabolism
                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e2013]:
                  - link "[191]" [ref=e2014] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-192"
                - text: The high level of similarity among the
                - link "metabolism" [ref=e2016] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolism
                - text: of mammals allows many of these feline diseases to be diagnosed using
                - link "genetic tests" [ref=e2017] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_testing
                - text: that were originally developed for use in humans, as well as the use of cats as
                - link "animal models" [ref=e2018] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_model
                - text: in the study of the human diseases.
                - superscript [ref=e2019]:

                    - /url: "#cite_note-194"
                - text: Diseases affecting domestic cats include acute infections,
                - link "parasitic infestations" [ref=e2025] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitic_disease
                - text: ", injuries, and chronic diseases such as"
                - link "kidney disease" [ref=e2026] [cursor=pointer]:

                - text: ","
                - link "hyperthyroidism" [ref=e2027] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feline_hyperthyroidism
                - text: ", and"
                - link "arthritis" [ref=e2028] [cursor=pointer]:

                - text: .
                - link "Vaccinations" [ref=e2029] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feline_vaccination
                - text: are available for many infectious diseases, as are treatments to eliminate parasites such as worms, ticks, and fleas.

          - region [ref=e2033]:
            - heading "Health issues" [level=2] [ref=e2035]
            - paragraph [ref=e2036]:
              - text: Between 50% and 90% of cats experience
              - link "dental" [ref=e2037] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_pathology
              - text: or
              - link "gum" [ref=e2038] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gums
              - text: problems, but these can be prevented by maintaining the cat's
              - link "oral hygiene" [ref=e2039] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_hygiene
              - text: using products specifically designed for cats, which are not toxic for them.
              - superscript [ref=e2040]:
                - link "[195]" [ref=e2041] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-CollegeDental-196"
              - text: Accidental
              - link "poisoning" [ref=e2043] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisoning
              - text: "in cats is common and can result from several sources: plants that are toxic to cats,"
              - link "medications" [ref=e2044] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medications
              - text: not intended for cats, foods unsuitable for cats, and household substances such as pesticides and household cleaners.
              - superscript [ref=e2045]:
                - link "[196]" [ref=e2046] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-CollegeHazards-197"
              - text: Plants toxic to cats include
              - link "lilies" [ref=e2048] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilium
              - text: ","
              - link "tulips" [ref=e2049] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulip
              - text: ", and"
              - link "philodendrons" [ref=e2050] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philodendron
              - text: ; medication poisoning occurs when cats ingest drugs intended for human, such as
              - link "acetaminophen" [ref=e2051] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetaminophen
              - text: and
              - link "aspirin" [ref=e2052] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aspirin
              - text: ", as well as vitamin capsules, flea treatments designed for dogs, and foods dangerous to cats like"
              - link "grapes" [ref=e2053] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grapes
              - text: ","
              - link "onions" [ref=e2054] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onions
              - text: ","
              - link "garlic" [ref=e2055] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garlic
              - text: ", and"
              - link "chocolate" [ref=e2056] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: .
              - superscript [ref=e2057]:

            - paragraph [ref=e2060]:
              - text: Cat owners' attitudes and knowledge affects how they care for their cats, and people with greater knowledge about cats are less likely to use
              - link "positive punishment" [ref=e2061] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positive_punishment
              - text: ", i.e. causing an unpleasant"
              - link "stimulus" [ref=e2062] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulus_(psychology)
              - text: to the cat.
              - superscript [ref=e2063]:
                - link "[197]" [ref=e2064] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Grigg2019-198"
              - text: Several organizations have published guidelines for the proper and safe care of cats. The
              - link "American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals" [ref=e2066] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_for_the_Prevention_of_Cruelty_to_Animals
              - text: has published a general guide emphasizing proper cat care, which covers appropriate
              - link "nutrition" [ref=e2067] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrition
              - text: and needs for fresh and clean water,
              - link "coat" [ref=e2068] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_coat
              - text: care, litter box maintenance, regular veterinary care.
              - superscript [ref=e2069]:
                - link "[198]" [ref=e2070] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-ASPCAgeneral-199"
              - text: The American Association of Feline Practitioners and the International Society of Feline Medicine released a guide on environmental needs of cats.
              - superscript [ref=e2072]:
                - link "[199]" [ref=e2073] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Ellis2013-200"
              - text: Professional organizations have emphasized the importance of
              - link "environmental enrichment" [ref=e2075] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_enrichment
              - text: for cats,
              - superscript [ref=e2076]:
                - link "[199]" [ref=e2077] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Ellis2013-200"
              - text: and some authors have raised concerns that many cat owners do not provide sufficient environmental enrichment. In an online survey of cat owners, only about half of the respondents reported playing with their cats daily.
              - superscript [ref=e2079]:
                - link "[197]" [ref=e2080] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Grigg2019-198"
            - paragraph [ref=e2082]:
              - text: Guidelines have also been published for
              - link "veterinarians" [ref=e2083] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veterinarians
              - text: and caregivers to improve the
              - link "welfare" [ref=e2084] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_welfare
              - text: of cats under their care, including recommendations for cat-friendly interactions in veterinary clinics.
              - superscript [ref=e2085]:
                - link "[200]" [ref=e2086] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Rodan2022-201"
              - text: "The guide focuses on five main aspects: providing a safe private space for the cat (e.g., a"
              - link "cardboard" [ref=e2088] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardboard
              - text: box on its side, placed in a high location, and in sufficient numbers if multiple cats are present); offering multiple environmental resources (several feeding stations, resting areas and litter boxes, and separating food from water); opportunities for play and activities that simulate
              - link "hunting behavior" [ref=e2089] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#Hunting_and_feeding"
              - text: (using appropriate toys and puzzle feeders); positive, consistent, and predictable social interaction (acclimating the cat to frequent contact from an early age, speaking softly, and avoiding forced contact); and an environment that allows the cat to use its sense of smell normally (providing scratching posts and other items where it can leave its
              - link "scent" [ref=e2090] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scent
              - text: ", and avoiding strong odors throughout the home)."
              - superscript [ref=e2091]:
                - text: "["

                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed

                - link "cosmopolitan species" [ref=e2108] [cursor=pointer]:

                - superscript [ref=e2109]:

                - link "Antarctica" [ref=e2112] [cursor=pointer]:

                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e2121]:

                - link "hybridization" [ref=e2132] [cursor=pointer]:

          - region [ref=e2220]:
            - heading "Interaction with humans" [level=2] [ref=e2222]
            - note [ref=e2223]:

            - paragraph [ref=e2229]:
              - text: Cats are common
              - link "pets" [ref=e2230] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet
              - text: throughout the world, and their worldwide population as of 2007 exceeded 500 million.
              - superscript [ref=e2231]:

              - text: As of 2024, the domestic cat was the second most popular pet in the United States, with 73.8 million cats owned and around 42.2 million households owning at least one cat.
              - superscript [ref=e2234]:

              - superscript [ref=e2237]:
                - link "[219]" [ref=e2238] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: In the United Kingdom, 26% of adults have a cat, with an estimated population of 10.9 million pet cats as of 2020.
              - superscript [ref=e2240]:
                - link "[220]" [ref=e2241] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-221"
              - text: As of 2021, there were an estimated 220 million owned and 480 million stray cats in the world.
              - superscript [ref=e2243]:
                - link "[221]" [ref=e2244] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-222"
            - paragraph [ref=e2246]:
              - text: Cats have been used for millennia to control rodents, notably
              - link "around grain stores" [ref=e2247] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farm_cat
              - text: and
              - link "aboard ships" [ref=e2248] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship's_cat
              - text: ", and both uses extend to the present day."
              - superscript [ref=e2249]:
                - link "[222]" [ref=e2250] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-223"
              - superscript [ref=e2252]:
                - link "[223]" [ref=e2253] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-224"
              - text: Cats are also used in the international
              - link "fur trade" [ref=e2255] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fur_trade
              - superscript [ref=e2256]:
                - link "[224]" [ref=e2257] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-225"
              - text: and leather industries for making coats, hats, blankets, stuffed toys,
              - superscript [ref=e2259]:
                - link "[225]" [ref=e2260] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-226"
              - text: shoes, gloves, and musical instruments.
              - superscript [ref=e2262]:
                - link "[226]" [ref=e2263] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-227"
              - text: About 24 cats are needed to make a cat-fur coat.
              - superscript [ref=e2265]:
                - link "[227]" [ref=e2266] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-228"
              - text: This use has been outlawed in the United States since 2000 and in the European Union (as well as the United Kingdom) since 2007.
              - superscript [ref=e2268]:
                - link "[228]" [ref=e2269] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-229"
            - paragraph [ref=e2271]:
              - text: Cat pelts have been used for superstitious purposes as part of the practice of
              - link "witchcraft" [ref=e2272] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witchcraft
              - text: ","
              - superscript [ref=e2273]:
                - link "[229]" [ref=e2274] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-230"
              - text: and they are still made into blankets in Switzerland as
              - link "traditional medicines" [ref=e2276] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_medicine
              - text: thought to cure
              - link "rheumatism" [ref=e2277] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheumatism
              - text: .
              - superscript [ref=e2278]:
                - link "[230]" [ref=e2279] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-231"
            - paragraph [ref=e2281]:
              - text: A few attempts to build a cat census have been made over the years, both through associations or national and international organizations (such as that of the
              - link "Canadian Federation of Humane Societies" [ref=e2282] [cursor=pointer]:

                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Chandoha
              - text: made his career photographing cats after his 1949 images of Loco, a stray cat, were published. He is reported to have photographed 90,000 cats during his career and maintained an archive of 225,000 images that he drew from for publications during his lifetime.
              - superscript [ref=e2308]:

            - paragraph [ref=e2311]:
              - link "Pet humanization" [ref=e2312] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: is a form of
              - link "anthropomorphism" [ref=e2313] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropomorphism
              - text: in which cats are kept for companionship and treated more like human family members than traditional pets.

              - text: This trend of
              - link "pet culture" [ref=e2317] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet_culture
              - text: involves providing cats with a higher level of care, attention and often even luxury, similar to the way humans are treated.

            - region [ref=e2321]:
              - heading "Shows" [level=3] [ref=e2323]

                - text: A
                - link "cat show" [ref=e2327] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_show
                - text: is a judged event in which the owners of cats compete to win titles in various cat-registering organizations by entering their cats to be judged after a breed standard.
                - superscript [ref=e2328]:
                  - link "[242]" [ref=e2329] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-How_Stuff_Works-2008-243"
                - text: It is often required that a cat must be healthy and vaccinated to participate in a cat show.
                - superscript [ref=e2331]:

                - link "pedigreed" [ref=e2334] [cursor=pointer]:

                - text: and non-
                - link "purebred" [ref=e2335] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purebred
                - text: companion ("moggy") cats are admissible, although the rules differ depending on the organization. Competing cats are compared to the applicable breed standard, and assessed for temperament.
                - superscript [ref=e2336]:

            - region [ref=e2339]:
              - heading "Infection" [level=3] [ref=e2341]
              - note [ref=e2342]:
                - text: "Main article:"
                - link "Feline zoonosis" [ref=e2343] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feline_zoonosis
              - paragraph [ref=e2344]:
                - text: Cats can be infected or infested with
                - link "viruses" [ref=e2345] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virus
                - text: ","
                - link "pathogenic bacteria" [ref=e2346] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogenic_bacteria
                - text: ","
                - link "fungus" [ref=e2347] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus
                - text: ","
                - link "protozoans" [ref=e2348] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protozoans
                - text: ","
                - link "arthropods" [ref=e2349] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod
                - text: or worms that can transmit diseases to humans; infections of most concern include
                - link "salmonella" [ref=e2350] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salmonella
                - text: ","
                - link "cat-scratch disease" [ref=e2351] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat-scratch_disease
                - text: ", and"
                - link "toxoplasmosis" [ref=e2352] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxoplasmosis
                - text: .
                - superscript [ref=e2353]:
                  - link "[243]" [ref=e2354] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Chomel2014-244"
                - text: In some cases, the cat exhibits no
                - link "symptoms" [ref=e2356] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symptoms
                - text: of the disease.
                - superscript [ref=e2357]:
                  - link "[244]" [ref=e2358] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Ohio2016-245"
                - text: The same disease can then become evident in a human.
                - superscript [ref=e2360]:
                  - link "[245]" [ref=e2361] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-Goldstein2015-246"
                - text: The likelihood that a person will become diseased depends on the age and
                - link "immune status" [ref=e2363] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immunocompetence
                - text: of the person. Others might also acquire infections from cat
                - link "feces" [ref=e2364] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feces
                - text: and
                - link "parasites" [ref=e2365] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasite
                - text: exiting the cat's body.

            - paragraph [ref=e2416]:
              - text: In
              - link "ancient Egypt" [ref=e2417] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egypt
              - text: ", cats were"
              - link "revered" [ref=e2418] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_worship
              - text: . The goddess
              - link "Bastet" [ref=e2419] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bastet
              - text: was often depicted in cat form, sometimes taking on the war-like aspect of a lioness. The Greek historian
              - link "Herodotus" [ref=e2420] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herodotus
              - text: reported that killing a cat was forbidden, and when a household cat died, the entire family mourned and shaved their eyebrows. Families took their dead cats to the sacred city of
              - link "Bubastis" [ref=e2421] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubastis
              - text: ", where they were embalmed and buried in sacred repositories. Herodotus expressed astonishment at the domestic cats in Egypt, because he had only ever seen wildcats."
              - superscript [ref=e2422]:
                - link "[40]" [ref=e2423] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Malek1997-41"
            - paragraph [ref=e2425]:
              - text: Ancient Greeks and Romans kept
              - link "weasels" [ref=e2426] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weasel
              - text: as pets, which were seen as the ideal rodent-killers. The earliest unmistakable evidence of the Greeks having domestic cats comes from two coins from
              - link "Magna Graecia" [ref=e2427] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna_Graecia
              - text: dating to the mid-fifth century BC showing Iokastos and Phalanthos, the legendary founders of
              - link "Rhegion" [ref=e2428] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggio_Calabria
              - text: and
              - link "Taras" [ref=e2429] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taranto
              - text: respectively, playing with their pet cats. The usual ancient Greek word for 'cat' was
              - generic "Ancient Greek (to 1453)-language text" [ref=e2430]: ailouros
              - text: ", meaning 'thing with the waving tail'. Cats are rarely mentioned in"
              - link "ancient Greek literature" [ref=e2431] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek_literature
              - text: .
              - link "Aristotle" [ref=e2432] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristotle
              - text: remarked in his
              - link "History of Animals" [ref=e2434] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Animals
              - text: that "female cats are naturally
              - link "lecherous" [ref=e2435] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promiscuity
              - text: "\". The Greeks later"
              - link "syncretized" [ref=e2436] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpretatio_graeca
              - text: their own goddess
              - link "Artemis" [ref=e2437] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artemis
              - text: with the Egyptian goddess Bastet, adopting Bastet's associations with cats and ascribing them to Artemis. In
              - link "Ovid" [ref=e2438] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovid
              - text: "'s"
              - link "Metamorphoses" [ref=e2440] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphoses
              - text: ", when the deities flee to Egypt and take animal forms, the goddess"
              - link "Diana" [ref=e2441] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_(mythology)
              - text: turns into a cat.
              - superscript [ref=e2442]:
                - link "[248]" [ref=e2443] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-Engels2001-249"
              - superscript [ref=e2445]:
                - link "[249]" [ref=e2446] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#cite_note-250"
            - paragraph [ref=e2448]:
              - text: Cats eventually displaced
              - link "weasels" [ref=e2449] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weasel
              - text: as the pest control of choice because they were more pleasant to have around the house and were more enthusiastic hunters of mice. During the
              - link "Middle Ages" [ref=e2450] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages
              - text: ", many of Artemis's associations with cats were grafted onto the"
              - link "Virgin Mary" [ref=e2451] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: . Cats are often shown in icons of
              - link "Annunciation" [ref=e2452] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: and of the
              - link "Holy Family" [ref=e2453] [cursor=pointer]:

              - link "Italian folklore" [ref=e2454] [cursor=pointer]:

              - link "Bethlehem" [ref=e2456] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethlehem
              - text: gave birth to a kitten.
              - superscript [ref=e2457]:

              - text: Several ancient religions believed cats are exalted souls, companions or guides for humans, that are all-knowing but mute so they cannot influence decisions made by humans. In Japan, the
              - generic "Japanese-language text" [ref=e2468]:

              - text: . The cat was once partnering with the first dog before the latter broke an oath they had made which resulted in enmity between the descendants of these two animals. It is also written that neither cats nor
              - link "foxes" [ref=e2482] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox
              - text: are represented in the water, while every other animal has an incarnation species in the water.
              - superscript [ref=e2483]:

              - text: Although no species are sacred in Islam,
              - link "cats are revered by Muslims" [ref=e2486] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_and_cats
              - text: . Some Western writers have stated
              - link "Muhammad" [ref=e2487] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad
              - text: had a favorite cat,
              - link "Muezza" [ref=e2489] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: .
              - superscript [ref=e2490]:
                - link "[254]" [ref=e2491] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: He is reported to have loved cats so much, "he would do without his cloak rather than disturb one that was sleeping on it".
              - superscript [ref=e2493]:
                - link "[255]" [ref=e2494] [cursor=pointer]:

              - text: saint,
              - link "Ahmed ar-Rifa'i" [ref=e2497] [cursor=pointer]:

              - superscript [ref=e2498]:

              - text: ("father of the kitten"), in reference to his documented affection to cats.

                    - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_De_Morgan
                  - text: depicting a
                  - link "witch" [ref=e2515] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witch
                  - text: with a black cat.
              - paragraph [ref=e2516]:
                - text: Many cultures have negative
                - link "superstitions" [ref=e2517] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstition
                - text: about cats. For example, that encountering a
                - link "black cat" [ref=e2518] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_cat
                - text: ("crossing one's path")
                - superscript [ref=e2519]:
                  - link "[258]" [ref=e2520] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-259"
                - text: leads to bad luck, or that cats are witches'
                - link "familiar spirits" [ref=e2522] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Familiar_spirit
                - text: used to augment a witch's powers and skills. The killing of cats in medieval
                - link "Ypres" [ref=e2523] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ypres
                - text: ", Belgium, is commemorated in the innocuous present-day"
                - link "Kattenstoet" [ref=e2524] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattenstoet
                - text: (cat parade).
                - superscript [ref=e2525]:
                  - link "[259]" [ref=e2526] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-260"
              - paragraph [ref=e2528]:
                - text: According to a myth in many cultures, cats have multiple lives. In many countries, they are believed to have nine lives, but in Italy, Germany, Greece, Brazil, and some Spanish-speaking regions, they are said to have seven lives,
                - superscript [ref=e2529]:
                  - link "[260]" [ref=e2530] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-261"
                - superscript [ref=e2532]:
                  - link "[261]" [ref=e2533] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-262"
                - text: while in Arabic traditions, the number of lives is six.
                - superscript [ref=e2535]:
                  - link "[262]" [ref=e2536] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-263"
                - text: An early mention of the myth is in
                - link "John Heywood" [ref=e2538] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Heywood
                - text: "'s The Proverbs of John Heywood (1546):"
                - superscript [ref=e2539]:
                  - link "[263]" [ref=e2540] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-264"
              - blockquote [ref=e2542]:
                - paragraph [ref=e2544]:
                  - text: Husband, (
                  - link "quoth" [ref=e2545] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/quoth#Verb_2
                  - text: she), ye studie, be merrie now, And even as ye thinke now, so come to yow. Nay not so, (quoth he), for my thought to tell right, I thinke how you lay
                  - link "groning" [ref=e2546] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/groning#English
                  - text: ", wife, all last night. Husband, a groning horse and a groning wife Never faile their master, (quoth she), for my life. No wife,"
                  - generic [ref=e2547]:
                    - text: a woman
                    - link "hath" [ref=e2548] [cursor=pointer]:
                      - /url: https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/hath#English
                    - text: nine lives like a cat
                  - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=e2549]:
                - text: The myth is attributed to the natural suppleness and swiftness cats exhibit to escape life-threatening situations.
                - superscript [ref=e2550]:
                  - link "[264]" [ref=e2551] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: "#cite_note-265"
                - text: Falling cats often land on their feet, using an instinctive
                - link "righting reflex" [ref=e2553] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat_righting_reflex
                - text: to twist their bodies around.
                - superscript [ref=e2554]:
                  - link "[265]" [ref=e2555] [cursor=pointer]:
